name: Society and Technology
description:
This course is designed to introduce non-social scientists to ‘the social’ and ‘society’. Before we get to the specific role of ‘data’ and ‘technology’ in society, we need to understand how people live together, how they interact and how that becomes meaningful to them. Understanding society is very different from understanding a technical system. 

So the course starts with an introduction to social science epistemology. How can we know and understand social phenomena? We then gallop through a set of core social theories that help us to understand the different perspectives onto ‘the social’. This will cover some 20th century white dudes, but also something a little more up-to-date and infused with feminism and postcolonial critique. 

Once we have the basics, we will begin to look into the specifics of data, technology and risk.
